sections.heading: Glamsterdam Network Status
sections.summary: Devnet-12 successfully tested builder deposit cache at fork transition; devnet-8 stable under load; Hoodi shadow fork planned once all client releases land.
sections.body:
- Devnet-12 tested excessive builder deposits at the fork transition: over 30,000 deposits including 5,000 invalid builder deposits; all clients handled it successfully, confirming the builder deposit cache works.
- Devnet-8 is still running with basic load and a few validator timeouts, but nothing significant.
- A Hoodi shadow fork will be launched as soon as all client releases are available to verify everything works as expected.
- No concerns raised by client teams on current network status.

sections.heading: BPO Test Fork Renaming
sections.summary: BPO test forks will be rebased on Amsterdam and renamed; PRs open for Besu, Geth, and Nimbus-EL; four other clients need no changes.
sections.body:
- Current BPO transition test forks (BPO3, BPO4) use names that will collide with future real BPO forks; proposal to rename them (e.g., `AmsterdamToBPOIncrease`, `BPOIncreaseToBPODecrease`) and rebase on Amsterdam.
  - [ethereum/execution-specs#3597](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3597)
- No changes needed for Erigon, ethrex, Nethermind, and Reth.
- Draft PRs opened for Besu ([besu#11646](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/pull/11646)), Geth ([go-ethereum#35975](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/35975)), and Nimbus-EL ([nimbus-eth1#5012](https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth1/pull/5012)); client teams asked to review.
- No objections raised; clients asked to comment on the PRs if they have naming preferences.

sections.heading: Separating Builder and Validator Deposits
sections.summary: Consensus: fix will not be included before Hoodi; it would be prototyped and tested on a short-lived devnet after Hoodi without delaying mainnet.
sections.body:
- Justin Traglia revisited [consensus-specs#5736](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5736): Lido and other DVT/LST systems identified that the current builder onboarding logic allows a bad actor to redirect validator deposits to an attacker-controlled builder, and smart contracts cannot easily detect this.
  - Workarounds exist: disable deposits during the pending queue window, monitor and pause deposits, or update contracts.
- Justin proposed fixing the spec after Hoodi, testing on a short-lived devnet (like devnet-12), and not delaying mainnet.
- Potuz strongly opposed making the change while keeping the current Hoodi and mainnet schedule, citing a pattern of late-breaking consensus changes causing bugs; willing to fix it only if deadlines are extended.
- Dustin (Nimbus), Eitan (Lighthouse), and Matthew Keil (Lodestar) also opposed delaying Hoodi.
- Dima (Lido) argued the fix touches a one-time call function and could be tested quickly, but acknowledged the scheduling constraints.
- Matthew Keil noted Devcon timing and holiday scheduling would push mainnet past the new year if Hoodi slips even a few days.
- Justin Traglia confirmed the bug is a hypothetical attack and not worth delaying anything.
- Consensus: the fix will not be included in Hoodi; Hoodi schedule remains unchanged. The fix will be prototyped, merged after Hoodi, and tested on a short-lived devnet without delaying mainnet.

sections.heading: BAL Retention Period
sections.summary: EL BAL retention standardized at 14,299 epochs via EIPs#12347; PR to be merged so CLs can blind; reduction to 8,192 deferred to Hegota.
sections.body:
- Toni Wahrstätter presented [EIPs#12347](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12347) (from Nico Flaig): increases EL BAL retention from 3,533 to 14,299 epochs (HISTORY_PRUNE_EPOCHS), enabling CLs to blind BALs while still serving old payload requests.
- Per-client status:
  - Besu: 14,299 epochs merged ([besu#11417](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/pull/11417)), confirmed by Besu team.
  - Erigon: prunes at finality, regenerates on demand; full mode ~8,192 epochs.
  - ethrex: no pruning yet, work in progress.
  - Geth: keeps BALs forever (none below snap-sync pivot); no change needed.
  - Nethermind: PR merged ([nethermind#14609](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/14609)), confirmed by Łukasz.
  - Nimbus-EL: PR open, waiting on EIPs#12347 ([nimbus-eth1#4815](https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth1/pull/4815)).
  - Reth: currently in-memory only, 3,533 epochs, lost on restart ([reth#27293](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/issues/27293)).
- Nico Flaig raised a concern about non-finality: if retention is reduced further, ELs pruning data could make payloads unservable over P2P for CLs that dedupe unfinalized data.
  - Lodestar does not dedupe non-finalized data; Prysm blinds everything on GP and noted it would be non-trivial to change.
- Potuz suggested computing a bound on non-finality duration based on the inactivity leak and validator ejections; the EL retention should exceed that bound.
- Toni noted 14,299 is very conservative; [EIP-8252](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8252) may reduce it to 8,192 epochs in Hegota (the time to restore finality if ~79% of stake goes offline).
- Agreement: Toni will merge EIPs#12347; CL clients can proceed with blinding BALs; further reduction discussion deferred to Heze/Hegota.

sections.heading: Hegota Scoping Process Change
sections.summary: Barnabas proposed that unmerged EIPs stay off agendas and unsupported PFI'd EIPs default to DFI; discussion deferred to ACDE #248 Thursday.
sections.body:
- Barnabas introduced [pm#2275](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/2275): unmerged EIPs stay off call agendas; PFI'd EIPs without client support default to DFI.
- Barnabas suggested the process change should apply starting with I-Star (the CL upgrade after Heze), not retroactively during the current cycle.
- Nixo confirmed a priority list is being prepared with PandaOps and Steel, to be brought to ACDE #248 this Thursday.
- Everyone asked to review [EIP-7723](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-7723.md) (Network Upgrade Inclusion Stages) before Thursday.

sections.heading: Heze-devnet-2 and Hegota Devnet Planning
sections.summary: Heze-devnet-2 may include 10-second slots with 3+ CL clients ready; EL blob params to be aligned; hegota-devnet-1 EL scope deferred to next Monday.
sections.body:
- Heze-devnet-1 is stable; heze-devnet-2 is in planning.
- 3-4 CL clients have implemented shorter slots on top of Beta-4: Prysm, Lodestar, Lighthouse, and Teku.
- Barnabas proposed heze-devnet-2 with 10-second slot time, noting that devnet-2 without shorter slots offers slim improvement over devnet-1.
  - Justin Traglia initially said no shorter slots for devnet-2 (just beta.4), but Barnabas argued the client threshold agreed upon last week (3 clients) has been met.
- PR [consensus-specs#5743](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5743) (Barnabas's fix PR on top of Jihoon's quick slots PR [consensus-specs#5718](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5718)) fixes bugs in shorter slots that could be triggered at Heze genesis; needs merge before devnet-2.
  - Justin Traglia wants Jihoon to review, but Jihoon is out of office this week.
- felipe raised EL blob schedule alignment: ethrex implemented blob params from [execution-specs#3703](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3703) (12/18); genesis generator uses 14/21. All EL devs asked to check alignment.
- Bogota-devnet-1 (frames) is running and spamming frame transactions; frames breakout #7 scheduled for tomorrow.
- Spencer asked about hegota-devnet-0 before Mumbai and hegota-devnet-1 EL scope (EIP-8298, EIP-8131, EIP-8279, EIP-8253, EIP-4758); Barnabas suggested scoping heze-devnet-2 first.
- Spencer will bring hegota-devnet-1 EL scope to next Monday's call for lock-in.

sections.heading: CFI vs SFI and Consensus-Specs Merge Policy
sections.summary: Strong pushback against merging CFI'd EIPs into the main consensus-specs fork branch; agreement that only SFI'd EIPs belong there, with CFI'd ones on feature branches.
sections.body:
- Potuz raised concerns about EIPs being merged into the Heze folder on the consensus-specs main branch before being SFI'd, creating implicit SFI through sunk cost.
  - Cited quick slots as an example where CFI was contentious but code is being merged into the main fork branch.
- lightclient strongly agreed: the main branch should reflect SFI'd EIPs only; merging CFI'd EIPs creates dependency and implicit acceptance.
- Matthew Keil (Lodestar) argued quick slots specifically lacks broad consensus and has knock-on effects for future slot work and PQ coordination; merging it feels like "sneaking it past the goalie."
- Justin Traglia acknowledged the concern and noted that for previous upgrades, things were sometimes merged before SFI; agreed the process should be tightened.
- Nico Flaig and Jihoon clarified that quick slots is not actually merged into the consensus-specs Heze folder; Jihoon's PR remains open.
- Potuz and lightclient agreed that already-merged CFI'd EIPs should stay (cost of removal > cost of keeping), but going forward, the main fork branch should only contain SFI'd items.
- On execution-specs side, danceratopz confirmed nothing is merged to the main development branch until SFI.
- Maria Silva noted quick slots is relatively easy to undo (just set slot time back to 12s), unlike other protocol changes.
- felipe warned of a slippery slope where sunk cost in testing and implementation pushes EIPs toward SFI.
- Spencer suggested [EIP-7723](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-7723.md) should be updated to properly define what CFI means for spec merging.
- Discussion to continue at ACDE #248 on Thursday with Nixo's priority list.

sections.heading: discv5 Defaults Across EL Clients
sections.summary: All EL clients confirmed to have discv5 enabled by default; discv4 sunsetting to be discussed separately.
sections.body:
- Csaba confirmed the question is whether all EL clients have discv5 on by default for their Hoodi release.
- Per-client status (from --help flags, Oct 7):
  - Besu: discv4+discv5 since 26.10.0 ([besu#11344](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/pull/11344)), confirmed by Besu team.
  - Erigon: discv5 default (discv4 behind a switch).
  - ethrex: discv4 + discv5, confirmed by Iván.
  - Geth: discv4 + discv5.
  - Nethermind: discv4 + discv5, confirmed by Łukasz.
  - Nimbus-EL: discv5 only.
  - Reth: discv4 + discv5.
- All clients have discv5 enabled; sunsetting discv4 to be discussed separately.
- Csaba noted Reth may have some failed discv5 hive tests, possibly from recently added tests; asked Reth team to check https://hive.ethpandaops.io/#/group/generic?suites=discv5.

sections.heading: EELS Hive Simulators as Prebuilt Docker Images
sections.summary: Hive simulator builds will drop from 100+ seconds to seconds using prebuilt images; client CI PRs open for Erigon, ethrex, Nethermind, and Reth.
sections.body:
- Spencer and danceratopz implemented prebuilt Docker images for execution-specs hive simulators, replacing per-run builds.
  - Build time drops from ~2 minutes to seconds; select releases with `--sim.buildarg tag=<tag>` (e.g., `v21.0.1`, `latest`, `nightly`, `<name>-devnet-<n>`).
- Core PRs: [execution-specs#3572](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3572) and [hive#1609](https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/1609), about to merge.
- Client CI PRs pushed by Spencer, review requested:
  - Erigon: [erigon#25061](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/25061)
  - ethrex: [ethrex#7432](https://github.com/lambdaclass/ethrex/pull/7432)
  - Nethermind: [nethermind#14898](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/14898)
  - Reth: [reth#28021](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28021)
- Besu, Geth, and Nimbus-EL can switch hive runs to `--sim.buildarg tag=<tag>` immediately.
- Spencer warned that merging may break client CI if they run Hive; backwards compatibility being evaluated.
